subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated same-command nonzero exec outcomes count as no progress from structured failure facts alone, even when their output text changes?
rationale: That choice fixes the observed runaway loop but deliberately trades output-sensitive retry availability for a bounded circuit breaker, and repository policy treats blocking behavior as a maintainer decision.

options.title: Accept structured failure identity
options.body: Land the current policy after rebase and exact-head gates, accepting that changing nonzero output does not reset the streak when exit facts remain the same.

options.title: Narrow the failure normalization
options.body: Require an additional stable semantic discriminator for completed nonzero exits before ignoring all output, reducing false blocks but risking more loop evasions.

options.title: Keep output-sensitive nonzero exits
options.body: Do not merge this behavior and leave the canonical runaway-loop issue unresolved until a different progress signal is designed.

recommendation.title: Accept structured failure identity
recommendation.body: Land the current policy after rebase and exact-head gates, accepting that changing nonzero output does not reset the streak when exit facts remain the same.

likelyOwner.reason: They performed the concrete runtime-contract review on this PR and are the strongest current routing signal for the exec producer and loop-detection boundary.
